problem.h2: Why teams want an alternative to Burnt AI
problem.lead: Burnt calls itself an AI watchtower for food distribution. It gives each team its own AI agent, software that handles one job: one takes in orders, one handles purchasing, and one calls customers about money they owe. It is a serious piece of engineering, and a Burnt AI alternative search rarely means it has failed. The question behind it is narrower: who should confirm what a kitchen asked for?

cards.h3: Software decides when a person looks
cards.body: Burnt's own page says it uses confidence thresholds to decide when a person must review an order, so the software flags the ones it is unsure of. That is a sensible design, but those flagged orders still land on your desk. Nowhere does it say the customer sees the order first.

cards.h3: A voicemail gets transcribed, not checked by the cook
cards.body: Burnt transcribes what comes in by phone or as a voicemail, which is genuinely useful. But the order begins as a loose message, and the cook who left it never sees the lines your system ends up holding.

cards.h3: Agents that work are worth keeping
cards.body: If Burnt's agents for orders, purchasing and collections already pay their way, pulling the platform out just to change who confirms an order would be a lot of disruption.

faq.h2: Burnt AI competitor, or an add-on beside it?

items.q: Should I look for a Burnt AI alternative just to let kitchens order by talking?
items.a: There is no need. Your Burnt agents can stay exactly as they are. VoiceOrder Solutions sits beside them as one more ordering option: the customer speaks it, checks it and sends it. Nothing has to be turned off.

items.q: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Burnt AI?
items.a: No, Burnt does far more, and it would be silly to pretend otherwise. Burnt reads channels we never touch and automates purchasing and invoice chasing, which we never go near. Our strength is different: the customer approves the order, so someone who knows that kitchen decides if it is right. If that is why you started looking for a Burnt AI alternative, you can add our app and keep Burnt.

items.q: Do the two products link up?
items.a: No. There is no connection between Burnt and our app, and no joint support. Their agents keep passing what they process into your system. Ours arrive separately, either emailed with a file or fed straight into your system.

items.q: Can our accounts still email or WhatsApp their orders?
items.a: Yes, and Burnt carries on reading them: it lists email, phone, voicemail, WhatsApp, SMS, EDI, portals and spreadsheets. We do not read incoming emails, texts, calls or other messages at all. A call that reaches your own desk carries no number from us, and no time stamp either: those come only with what is sent from our app.

items.q: How soon could our accounts be ordering?
items.a: Most distributors are up and running within 24 to 48 hours, and most kitchens place their first order on day one. Burnt keeps running throughout, so there is no switchover to schedule.

items.q: Will anyone need to come to our site?
items.a: Not for this. We set up from the guides you send over, with no implementation project. Burnt describes hands-on onboarding, with their team working at your site; if that already happened for your agents, adding us does not repeat it.

items.q: What does VoiceOrder Solutions cost if we keep Burnt?
items.a: Neither of us publishes a rate card. We quote per distributor once we know what you run, and Burnt quotes after a demo. Since the agents stay, the only figure to weigh is the price of adding our app.

items.q: Where do the Burnt details on this page come from?
items.a: Burnt's own website, read on 10 October 2026: the agent list and the on-site onboarding line off their homepage, and the channel list and the confidence-threshold wording off their sales and operations product page. We have left their accuracy and time-saving figures out, because those are their numbers to stand behind. If any of it has changed, this page is what needs correcting.
